title: Phase-plane sweep: latency vs cost vignette
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working vignette that describes a "phase-plane" style sweep of latency vs unit-cost across a small set of representative serving configurations. The goal is to produce collateral we can hand to product + SRE teams that explains the operational envelope (where configurations sit on the latency–cost plane) and the shape of iso-SLO contours for typical request mixes.

Scope and audience
- Audience: product managers, SREs, solutions engineers who need quick heuristics for config selection.
- Not intended as final benchmarking numbers for pricing — rather, directional and actionable tradeoffs.

Experimental setup (short)
- Model: openmix-13B (baseline) and openmix-7B (cheap variant).
- Hardware: A100-80GB (core) and T4 (edge proxy for small throughput).
- Variants: fp16, int8 (static 8-bit), q4_0 (4-bit quant), q4_1 (4-bit slightly lossy), and dynamic quant fallback toggled.
- Batch sizes tested: 1, 4, 16, 64 (sessionized requests), with a simple session muxer for session-affinity test.
- Workloads: convo (multi-turn chat, median length 340 tokens per request), short-gen (prompt 40 tokens), rerank (embedding-lite call).
- Metric windows: steady-state 30s windows after warmup. Costs are approximated unit costs using our cost model (GPU-minutes translated to $/k tokens).

High-level phase-plane ASCII summary (latency on Y in ms, cost on X in $ per 1k tokens):

Legend: 
 * FP16 = f16, I8 = int8, Q4 = 4-bit quant variant
 * B=N means batching size N, SLO lines show target p95 latency thresholds

    Cost ($/1k) --> 0.8    1.2    1.6    2.0    2.4
 Latency (ms)                                                                
  900 |                                                                      
  700 |    x(f16,B=1)                          o(I8,B=1)                     
  500 |                         + (q4,B=1)                                     
  350 |         * (f16,B=4)        . (i8,B=4)                                  
  250 |                    · (q4,B=4)                                           
  150 |         (f16,B=16)   (i8,B=16)   (q4,B=16)                              
   80 |   (f16,B=64)  (i8,B=64)  (q4,B=64)                                      
   40 | (7B-q4,B=64)                                                           

Notes on the sketch: points are approximate cluster centers from the sweep; q4 variants cluster toward lower-cost, lower-latency at larger batch sizes but can have higher p95 variance under bursty arrival.

Representative numeric slice (Convo workload, p95 latency, $/1k tokens):
- openmix-13B, fp16: B=1 -> p95 720 ms, cost 1.9 $/1k; B=16 -> p95 160 ms, cost 1.05 $/1k; B=64 -> p95 90 ms, cost 0.88 $/1k.
- openmix-13B, int8: B=1 -> p95 420 ms, cost 1.6 $/1k; B=16 -> p95 120 ms, cost 0.82 $/1k; B=64 -> p95 70 ms, cost 0.70 $/1k.
- openmix-13B, q4_1: B=1 -> p95 360 ms, cost 1.2 $/1k; B=16 -> p95 95 ms, cost 0.55 $/1k; B=64 -> p95 58 ms, cost 0.46 $/1k.
- openmix-7B, q4_1 (B=64) -> p95 42 ms, cost 0.25 $/1k (good baseline for low-SLA features).

Iso-SLO contour discussion (interpretation)
- For a 200 ms p95 SLO, many fp16 configs require large batching (B>=16) or are infeasible at small B. Int8 and q4 variants cross the 200 ms SLO at lower batching levels.
- Cost-optimal frontier for p95 <= 200 ms tends to be: use q4_1 at B=16 or B=64 for conversation workloads; if quality regression is unacceptable, fallback to int8 B=16.
- For p95 <= 80 ms (interactive UI), fp16+B=64 or q4+B=64 on smaller models is required; this is where edge proxies (T4) + model sharding give marginal gains.

Burst behavior and variance (qualitative)
- Cold-starts and KV cache misses cause spikes that disproportionately affect p95; q4 variants show larger p95 tail under burst because CPU fallback or dequantization stalls happen unpredictably.
- Under microbursts (sustained arrival > 5x baseline for 5–20s), batching helps reduce cost but raises immediate p95 — a tradeoff that depends on whether SLO is throughput-aware.
- Recommended mitigation: keep a small warm pool with pre-warmed sessions for high-SLA tenants and enable KV-prefix caching for long conversations.

Short text charts: cost vs batching (convo workload, q4_1):
- Batch size: 1 -> cost 1.2 $/1k, p95 360 ms
- Batch size: 4 -> cost 0.9 $/1k, p95 170 ms
- Batch size: 16 -> cost 0.55 $/1k, p95 95 ms
- Batch size: 64 -> cost 0.46 $/1k, p95 58 ms

Operational heuristics (first-draft)
1) If product needs p95 <= 150 ms and quality tolerant -> default to q4_1, B=16; fallback chain: q4_1 -> i8 -> fp16 (if degenerates).
2) If product requires strict quality (no quant regression), target int8, B=16 and review evals on long-context tests.
3) For UI interactions (<80 ms target), prefer smaller model (7B) q4 at B>=64 placed on edge proximity nodes; accept higher cost per token for latency benefits.
4) Have explicit guardrails in routing policy: a single request that trips p99 > 2x baseline should trigger instant fallback to higher-precision variant for subsequent requests from same session.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-up benchmarks)
- How do these contours shift for longer contexts (2k tokens)? Quick intuition: latency grows sublinearly for q4 vs fp16 because token compute dominates memory movement, but cache pressure increases. Need a 2k token sweep.
- Interaction with autoscaling: are burst penalties dominated by scale-up time or by cold KV-cache misses? Add scale simulation traces to next run.
- How reproducible are p95 clusters across instance families (H100 vs A100)? We have only A100 runs here.

Next steps and deliverables
- Run 2k-token sweep across fp16/int8/q4_1 on H100 and A100 (ENG-4821). Owner: Luca Morales. ETA: 2027-11-12.
- Produce a slide with a proper 2D phase-plane heatmap + iso-SLO contours for leadership. Owner: Priya Raman. ETA: 2027-11-17.
- Add burst-sim tests to testbed and run 100 synthetic microburst scenarios; capture p95/p99 and autoscale traces. Owner: Evan Brooks. ETA: 2027-11-24.

Appendix: quick thought experiment on pricing impact
- If product X needs p95 <= 200ms and we pick q4_1 B=16, estimated incremental cost vs default fp16 B=1 is ~ -0.85 $/1k (savings) while maintaining latency. For high-volume workloads this is material to pricing tiers.
